sections.label: Evidence selection
sections.short: Runs prepared search routes and chooses how many fused results are returned.
sections.long: Retrieval executes independently bounded lexical and vector channels. Final result limit is applied after fusion when evidence is returned; it does not alter BM25 or vector top-K.

variables.label: Final result limit
variables.short: Maximum fused evidence results returned for one query.
variables.long: Lexical and vector channels use separately prepared top-K values. After retrieval and reciprocal-rank fusion, the search tool returns at most this many evidence results to its caller.

sections.label: Result fusion
sections.short: Combines lexical and semantic channel rankings into one order.
sections.long: Reciprocal Rank Fusion adds one reciprocal contribution for every channel rank. Its rank constant controls contribution magnitude and the difference between early and later positions.

variables.label: RRF rank constant
variables.short: Controls how sharply reciprocal-rank fusion distinguishes early from later ranks.
variables.long: Each channel contributes weight divided by k plus rank. Lower k magnifies differences between early and later ranks; higher k flattens rank differences and increases the relative importance of agreement across channels.
